primary_grammar_sources.scope: University teaching examples corroborate first-person present liking, work expression, and sentence-initial Je question framing. Facts verify authored units; no full course passages imported.
Present possession contrasts nina and una; these are possession forms, not perfect auxiliaries.
Primary course indexed text describes subject-prefix/present/stem formation; direct page fetch403 retained as access limitation.

scope: Exact words contiguous, no external modal/do auxiliary; positive present I predicates. Question units only sentence-initial and one-to-one singular recipient assumed. Have requires bounded explicit nominal complement and qualified following boundary; perfect, obligation and causative forms are inapplicable.
limitations: Local guards are not a complete grammar or word-sense parser.
Finite predicates with English complements intentionally remain mixed language; target object agreement is not solved.
Question units do not claim plural recipient support.
Source absence and ambiguity are evaluated, not filled with model calls.
